description: The puzzle build's benchmark (scripts/puzzle_benchmark.py): the cases every branch is built on. FROZEN on 2026-11-17, before anything was tuned on them: a case is not changed, dropped or re-seeded to make a number better. The green puzzle (base3: two bars, two forks), Newton, SAM 3.1 looking, the pieces at the friction the checkout's own physics gives them. Seeds 21 and up: none of the seeds the build or its correction table were worked out on (1 to 6, 11 to 16).

scatter.what: The pieces anywhere in the region, 35 mm apart, the base 0.24 to 0.32 m to either side of the middle: as the build's own scatter lays them.

base_left.what: The base starts on the left of the middle; the pieces anywhere.

base_right.what: The base starts on the right of the middle; the pieces anywhere.

tight.what: The loose pieces close together: every middle within 0.13 m of one point, and 22 mm between pieces where the others have 35 mm. An open finger needs 18.4 mm.

far.what: Every loose piece in the far half of the table: beyond the middle line, away from the robot.

near.what: Every loose piece in the near half of the table: this side of the middle line, toward the robot, where the survey looks past its own gripper.

pieces_left.what: For the long carries: the base starts on the left of its target and every loose piece lies in the left third of the table.

in_view: Every layout lies inside region (x and y ranges of the table, metres), which is what the survey of every checkout compared sees from its pose, and outside hidden, the patches of it that a survey's own gripper hides: every piece is in view at the survey in every base case, whatever checkout builds it. A piece the scan does not find there is the loop's miss, not the layout's. Not so in the stretch cases that move the base's target outward.

disturbance.what: Made from outside the build, by scripts/puzzle_disturb.py, when the build prints the caption named; the build is not told. Recovered means every piece seated at the end and the graph ended in success.

base_moved.on_caption: line_red: carrying it over its slot

stretch.what: Reported, and outside the bar's rates: where the loop stops working.

reach_far.what: The base's target moved away from the robot in 40 mm steps until the build fails; the first is the build's own target.

reach_side.what: The base's target moved along the rail in 80 mm steps until the build fails.

long_carry.what: The base's target 0.24 m to the right of the middle and every loose piece in the left third of the table: each piece is carried 0.38 m or more.
